simulatedPerson.name: faces
simulatedPerson.hiddenRule: Likes close shots or shallow focus (85%); dislikes extreme wide shots (10%); otherwise 25%.

draftInterpretation: Across 83 stills from 35 films you liked 36 (43%). What follows compares the stills you liked with the ones you did not; it describes your choices in this collection, not a fixed type.

Clearly, shallow focus (only one plane is sharp; the rest is soft): you liked 16 of 17 (94%), against 30% of the rest, across 12 films. For example: 12 Angry Men: Juror 3; Amélie: Amélie in the café; In the Mood for Love: Mrs Chan sips from a green teacup in the red restaurant booth.

Clearly, interior (indoors): you liked 21 of 33 (64%), against 30% of the rest, across 16 films. For example: 12 Angry Men: Juror 3; Amélie: Amélie in the café; Double Indemnity: Keyes at his office door.

These cannot yet be told apart from the characteristics above, because they occur in nearly the same works: close shots with shallow focus, artificial light with shallow focus and side light with shallow focus.
Too few examples to say anything yet about vehicle (2 judged).

signature.summary: A clear leaning towards shallow focus and interior.

statements.text: Liked 16 of 17 works with shallow focus (94%), against 20 of 66 without it (30%).
Liked 21 of 33 works with interior (64%), against 15 of 50 without it (30%).

terminology.label: eye level
terminology.definition: The camera is at about the subject's eye height.

terminology.label: high angle
terminology.definition: The camera looks down on the subject.

terminology.label: high or low camera
terminology.definition: Any angle other than eye level: high, low, overhead or canted.

terminology.label: intimate
terminology.definition: Close and private.

terminology.label: serene
terminology.definition: Calm and still.

terminology.label: leading lines
terminology.definition: Lines in the set or landscape draw the eye towards a point.

terminology.label: off-centre subject
terminology.definition: The main subject is placed clearly to one side.

terminology.label: silhouette
terminology.definition: Subjects appear as dark shapes against a brighter background.

terminology.label: deep focus
terminology.definition: Near and far planes are both sharp.

terminology.label: shallow focus
terminology.definition: Only one plane is sharp; the rest is soft.

terminology.label: side light
terminology.definition: Light from one side, modelling form with shadow.

terminology.label: top light
terminology.definition: Light from above, shadowing eyes and lower forms.

terminology.label: artificial light
terminology.definition: Electric light from sources outside the frame.

terminology.label: daylight
terminology.definition: Sun or sky light.

terminology.label: exterior
terminology.definition: Outdoors.

terminology.label: interior
terminology.definition: Indoors.

terminology.label: close shots
terminology.definition: Any shot from medium close-up to extreme close-up: the frame is mostly face, body or object.

terminology.label: close-up
terminology.definition: A face or object fills most of the frame.

terminology.label: distant shots
terminology.definition: Wide and extreme wide shots: the setting dominates the figures.

terminology.label: medium close-up
terminology.definition: Head and shoulders.

limitations: Associations describe this person's judgments of this library only; they are not a comparison with other people.
Characteristics that always appear together in the works judged cannot be separated and are reported together.
Strength labels come from exact tests corrected for the number of characteristics tested; tentative findings may disappear with more judgments.
Findings marked subjective rest on atmosphere or tone readings, which are interpretations rather than observations.
